To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
during both signals (anticipating and trigger) of a complex conditioned signal, the functional states of brain struc-tures were equivalent, though the behaviour of the animals was different.

the functional states of structures of the limbic system and frontal cortex are equivalent during exposure to anticipanting and triggering signals of the complex conditioned stimulus, and that the food-procuring behavior is inhibited during exposure to the anticipanting signal.
the functional state of the hippocampus, amydgala and frontal cortex in the dog was higher during the anticipating signal than during the triggering signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional state of the brain structures under the influence of the anticipatory and trigger components of the conditioned stimulus.
the functional state of the brain structures under the action of a complex conditioned signal.
the problem of the role of the functional state of brain structures in the formation of the conditioned reflex and its functional significance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functional states of brain areas are determined by the functional state of the brain as a whole.
the functional state of brain structures is a key factor in the regulation of food-procuring behavior.
the functional state of brain structures is a factor that determines the nature of the reaction to a stimulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the functional state of a brain structure is a measure of the functional state of the entire brain.
the anticipatory signal is the most important factor in the formation of the conditioned reflex, and the trigger signal is the most effective factor in the manifestation of the conditioned reflex.
the anticipatory signal for feeding behaviour is characterized by the functional states of brain structure which are similar to the states under the action of trigger signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain structures functional states are not determined by the presence of a signal, but by its significance.
it’s possible to measure the functional states of brain regions and that these states change during exposure to different types of stimuli.
the functional state of brain structures during the anticipation of a signal is higher than during the trigger signal.
